claims.text: Adding 0.5–1 at.% yttrium to CoCrFeNiAl bond coats promotes yttrium segregation at grain boundaries during cyclic oxidation at 1100–1250°C.
Adding 0.5–1 at.% yttrium promotes yttrium segregation at the bond coat/oxide interface.
Yttrium segregation enables formation of adherent, Y-rich oxide scales.
Y-rich oxide scales enhance oxidation resistance.
Adding 0.5–1 at.% yttrium extends thermal-barrier-coating cyclic life by approximately 40–50% relative to an undoped CoCrFeNiAl bond coat.
The predicted benefit depends on the bond-coat microstructure remaining free of deleterious secondary phases.
Yttrium acts as a reactive element in the proposed bond-coat system.
Yttrium reduces vacancy mobility at critical interfaces.
Stabilized oxide growth and reduced interfacial vacancy mobility enhance oxide-scale adhesion.
Enhanced oxide-scale adhesion reduces spallation during cyclic oxidation.
Undoped HEA bond coats typically undergo earlier oxide-scale failure and spallation under high-temperature cyclic conditions than the proposed yttrium-doped coats.
The performance enhancement is expected to be confined to high-temperature cyclic oxidizing environments and may not occur under other operating conditions.
The reactive-element effect of yttrium is well documented in systems similar to the proposed HEA bond coat.
The exact behavior and optimal concentration of yttrium in CoCrFeNiAl HEA bond coats remain uncertain.
